about: What each log key means. Inputs are recorded readings, replayed as-is; outputs are computed, and replay recomputes them. <name> is filled in at runtime. Generated by tools/make_log_key_guide.py; do not edit.

advantageKit.doc: Driver Station and match data: enabled, mode, alliance, event, match number and type, joysticks (AdvantageKit)
Controller CPU, memory, storage, network, CAN bus, IMU, faults, battery, NT clients and clock validity (AdvantageKit)
Radio status JSON (AdvantageKit; Wi-Fi keys redacted by RadioStatusRedactor)
Loop timing: FullCycleMS, UserCodeMS, LogPeriodicMS, GC time (AdvantageKit)
Build and robot identity: GitSHA, GitBranch, BuildDate, RobotIdentity, BootId, LogKeyGuide
Values read from the dashboard over NetworkTables (LoggedNetwork*), recorded so replay sees what the robot saw
Tuned values from src/main/deploy/params/*.json and their dashboard overrides, by group and name (Params)
Code timings (Telemetry.time/timeEnd), once a second: the key is the worst span of that second, <key>Mean the mean. RobotPeriodic is the whole loop; Periodic/<Subsystem> each subsystem
The match summary (MatchSummary), once a second: battery, brownouts, loop, DS drops, CAN/<bus>/Drops|DownSeconds|BusOffs, Devices/*, Auto/*, Alerts/*, PeakTempC/<device>; see docs/match-summary.md

keys.doc: Whether the device is talking at all (NT heartbeat, frames arriving).

Per-tag data of this loop's frame, FIDUCIAL_STRIDE values per tag: id, horizontal and vertical angle from the principal point (deg, positive right and up), camera-to-tag distance (m), ambiguity. Limelight MegaTag1 only; empty otherwise.
Source-specific health numbers, e.g. QuestNav battery, Limelight fps. Keys fixed per IO.
Kind ordinal of this source's observations; -1 before the first.
Per-observation PoseObservation#stdDevScale; logged only when some entry isn't 1.
Every tag id seen this loop, for display.

Phoenix's fault bitfields (getFaultField, getStickyFaultField): active now, and latched since boot (sticky faults are cleared when the motor is created). The bit order is undocumented: Tuner X decodes it. troubleFaults names the ones that matter.
Position projected from the frame's own timestamp to the refresh, along the velocity.
The motor rebooted since last loop, so its position restarted and its signal rates went back to defaults. Not set for a device's first report after the program starts.
The leader's sticky faults that mean something went wrong (hardware, temperature, voltage, boot during enable), by name, e.g. Undervoltage. Never current or position limits.
A signal whose refresh failed is a motor that did not answer.
The constrained solve is native code; a failure drops this frame, not the loop.
Lets the web app tell "the numbers are not moving" apart from "the robot went away".
One entry per observation, in input order: the tier if accepted, the reason if not.
Empty on quiet loops so each event appears once, in the loop it happened.
Informational only: how far the fused heading is from the spot's heading. The set shot exists for when that heading cannot be trusted, so it never gates.
Fused heading minus the aim target, while the drivetrain aims; NaN for a set shot.
The one key on the dashboard: bursts counting up is how you know rows are being written.
(Pose, module targets/velocities and chassis speed are not re-logged here: they are Localization/FusedPose and the Swerve inputs ModuleTargets, ModuleVelocities and RobotVelocity already.)
An output, not metadata: AdvantageKit ignores recordMetadata after Logger.start().
An output, so a replay's log shows what the replay solved with.
Battery voltage, as the controller measured it.
The controller is browned out (outputs disabled). False where the API is unavailable.
Whether the recorded run was the desktop simulator (false on a robot).
Pigeon acceleration along its own axes, g (gravity included). All 0 when not read.
CTRE's own pose estimate, for comparison only.
Phoenix's raw Pigeon reset flag; logic reads Swerve.gyroRebootedThisLoop.
Per module: drive and steer motors both answering this loop.
Per module: Phoenix's raw reset flag for the drive motor, which is also true on the first contact after boot. Logic reads Swerve.moduleRebootedThisLoop instead.
Module steer angle per sample, radians, flattened.
Module drive distance per sample, metres, flattened.
Sample times, Timer.getTimestamp() base.
Gyro yaw per sample, radians.
Raw, m/s^2: WPILib does not apply the mount orientation to the accelerometer.
SystemCore's onboard IMU, the backup gyro. Not on CAN, so a CANivore drop spares it.
The Jetson's saved excluded tags plus the robot's (excludedTagsActive).
Why the Jetson could not load the robot's map, or empty.
Canonical hash of the field map the Jetson loaded and solves with; empty until reported.
When the Jetson loaded it, Jetson unix seconds.
+1 each second while PhotonVision runs.
-- /photonvision/jetson/, JetsonDiagnostics (SpectrumJetson patch 82) --
-- /photonvision/rewind/ --
Why the Jetson is slowing itself down: None, OVER-CURRENT, HIGH TEMP (...), ...
The Jetson's /proc/uptime; bootId changes on a reboot.
Camera matrix, row-major 3x3; empty until the camera has connected.
PhotonLib's isConnected(): the camera's heartbeat is on NetworkTables.
Distortion coefficients (the Jetson sends all 8); empty until connected.
PhotonLib's getEnabled(): false while turned off with setEnabled(false).
-- /photonvision/<camera>/health/ (section 9a), NaN / -1 until first published --
streaming, stalled, recovering, disconnected, gave-up, paused or starting (patch 81).
-- /photonvision/<camera>/mount/ (section 9b) --
The pipeline the camera reports running.
Results PhotonLib failed to read this loop (PhotonVision #2528); they were dropped.

Results the camera sent this loop, including any not logged in results: while the robot is disabled only the newest result with targets is kept, at 10 Hz, to keep the log small (the Orin feeds neither the pose nor the seed while disabled). Frame rate and the no-frames alert use this count.
Serialized PhotonPipelineResults, oldest first.
/photonvision/<camera>/settingsJson (section 11a); written to the log on change.
